problems.claim: `Dispatch_By_60F080` has 256 entries; 168 of them are a lone `ret`. Beyond the parts and the controllers, thirteen numbers — 0x44, 0x45, 0x46, 0x48, 0x60, 0x70, 0x72, 0x7A, 0x90, 0x91, 0x98, 0xA8, 0xB0 — have one handler each that is not decoded yet. (questions.md asks what they do; wsa1-disassembly says thirteen of the dispatcher's handlers are still sub_XXXXXX.)
problems.evidence: From the ROM table at 0xFAC8EA and wsa1/prom_a/wsa1_prom_a.s, nine of the thirteen go to a handler that is only `ret`: 0x44/0x45/0x46 all go to sub_FABB5D (`ret` at 0xFABB5D, so the three share one handler), 0x48 to sub_FABB60, 0x90 to sub_FABBCF, 0x91 to sub_FABBD0, 0x60 to sub_FABBD2, 0x70 to sub_FABBD4 and 0x72 to sub_FABBD5, each a bare `ret`. Only 0x7A (sub_FABB61), 0x98 (sub_FABBD7), 0xA8 (sub_FABCD7) and 0xB0 (sub_FABCEF) have bodies. So 177 of the 256 entries do nothing, not 168, and there are 11 distinct handlers for the 13 numbers, not 13.
problems.fix: Say: 168 entries point at the shared `ret` sub_FAC845. Nine more numbers (0x44–0x46, 0x48, 0x60, 0x70, 0x72, 0x90, 0x91) point at their own one-byte `ret` stubs, so they are no-ops in this dispatcher too. Only 0x7A, 0x98, 0xA8 and 0xB0 have handlers with bodies, and those are not decoded. Narrow the questions.md item to those four, and reword the wsa1-disassembly count to match.
